newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares edge up to 16-month high.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares edge up to 16-month high.

text.p: Egyptian shares edged up to another 16-month high on Wednesday in trading still dominated by cement and milling stocks, brokers said.
The Capital Markets Authority (CMA) overall index closed 0.01 points up at 235.04 points, its highest since late April 1995, on volume of 142.52 million pounds ($41.92 million).
Turnover was up significantly through registration of 375,000 shares in Misr International Bank, sold off this week by state-owned Banque Misr at a fixed 310 pounds each.
"More increases are still expected," Youssef Khalil of Delta EAB told Reuters, "because the cash available surpasses the market's capacity."
Cement and milling firms, the market's favourites, performed well.
Suez Cement closed 0.45 pounds up at 46.70 after shares worth 5.48 million pounds changed hands.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement and Helwan Portland Cement rose 0.50 pounds to close at 57.50 and 44.50 respectively.
Egyptians Abroad for Investment and Development was the market leader, finishing 1.75 pounds up at 17.75 on volume of 6.86 million pounds.
North Cairo Flour Mills rose 1.00 pound to finally reach the 100.00 pound level.
Among other popular millers, Southern Cairo Flour Mills finished the day 1.50 pounds higher at 52.50.
Kafr el-Zayat Pesticides and Chemicals, the recently privatised and heavily oversubscribed share, continued its uptrend, rising 0.80 pounds to finish at 48.50.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 350.95 points from 349.22 on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose slightly to 160.74 from 160.73.
